Schedule 5 Flight test standards

The following Table of Contents is for guidance only and is not part of the Schedule.

### Table of Contents

Section G Recreational pilot licence (RPL)Appendix G.1 RPL Aeroplane category rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a recreational pilot licence with aeroplane category rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the recreational pilot licence with aeroplane category rating;

applicability of drug and alcohol regulations;

aircraft instrument requirements for VFR operations;

emergency equipment requirements;

fuel planning and oil requirements for the flight;

managing passengers and the carriage of cargo;

aircraft speed limitations;

aircraft systems.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection;

refuel an aeroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A2, C3 and IFF.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

taxi an aeroplane;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a cross-wind take-off;

conduct a short-field take-off;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following: maximum rate climb; maximum angle climb; cruise climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn an aeroplane;

navigate and transit from a circuit area to a training area and return;

operate safely in local area airspace;

establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following configurations: turbulence; flaps selected; high speed.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A5, A6 and IFF.

enter and recover from each of the following flight conditions, 1 of which must be in the approach configuration: a fully developed stall; a wing drop at the stall;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes;

manage an engine failure after take-off;

manage the following malfunctions: a malfunction during start or shutdown; and any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i): an aircraft system malfunction; engine or cabin fire; radio failure;

perform a forced landing.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

conduct descents maintaining a constant heading and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, A4 and A6.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct a cross-wind landing;

conduct short-field and flapless landings;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1 and C2.

park, shutdown, and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the test;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; simulated carriage of passengers and cargo; a simulated private local area operation; operating in Class G airspace, at a non-towered aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in an aeroplane; conducted by day under the VFR; operating at a non-towered aerodrome may be simulated if the test is conducted at a controlled aerodrome; if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the AFM, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres may be taken from the applicant’s training records.

Appendix G.2 RPL Helicopter category rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a recreational pilot licence with helicopter category rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the recreational pilot licence with helicopter category rating;

applicability of drug and alcohol regulations;

aircraft instrument requirements for VFR operations;

emergency equipment requirements;

fuel planning and oil requirements for the flight;

managing passengers and the carriage of cargo;

aircraft speed limitations;

aircraft systems.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection;

refuel a helicopter (may be assessed by questioning).

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H1, H2, H3, H4 and H5.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

lift-off and hover a helicopter;

taxi a helicopter;

air transit a helicopter;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct climbs on a constant heading, and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following: maximum rate climb; maximum angle climb; cruise climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code H5.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn a helicopter;

navigate and transit from a circuit area to a training area and return;

operate safely in local area airspace.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H2, H6 and H7.

hover a helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions and perform turns around 1 of the following: rotor mast; helicopter nose; helicopter tail;

perform sidewards and backwards flight;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform an autorotative flight manoeuvre;

land on and lift off from sloping ground;

land, manoeuvre, and take off in a confined area;

execute a limited power take-off, approach and landing;

perform a forced landing;

manage an engine failure during hover or taxi;

manage a control or tail rotor malfunction in flight and at the hover (simulated);

manage at least 1 of the following: an engine fire; electrical failure; hydraulic system malfunction; airframe fuel system malfunction; engine governor system malfunction.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H5.

conduct descents maintaining a constant heading and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome or helicopter landing site arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H3, H4 and H5.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct an approach to the hover;

conduct a helicopter air transit;

perform a go-around procedure.

**Post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code C2.

park, shutdown and secure the helicopter;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the test;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; simulated carriage of passengers and cargo; a simulated private local area operation; operating in Class G airspace and at a non-towered aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a helicopter; conducted by day under the VFR; operating at a non-towered aerodrome may be simulated if the test is conducted at a controlled aerodrome; assessment of competency for activities and manoeuvres that require the applicant to operate the helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions may be taken from the applicant’s training records if the conditions are insufficient.

Appendix G.3 RPL Gyroplane category rating flight test

1\. Flight test requirements

An applicant for a recreational pilot licence with gyroplane category rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

(a) knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

(b) ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

2\. Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the following topics are listed:

(a) privileges and limitations of the recreational pilot licence with gyroplane category rating;

(b) applicability of drug and alcohol regulations;

(c) aircraft instrument requirements for VFR operations;

(d) emergency equipment requirements;

(e) fuel planning and oil requirements for the flight;

(f) managing passengers and the carriage of cargo;

(g) aircraft speed limitations;

(h) aircraft systems.

3 Activities and manoeuvres

**3.1** For paragraph 1 (b), the activities and manoeuvres set out in subclauses 3.2 to 3.9 are mentioned.

*Note* The activities and manoeuvres are not required to be conducted in the order in which they appear in this Appendix.

3.2 Pre-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

(a) perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

(b) perform pre-flight inspection;

(c) refuel a gyroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

3.3 Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G2 and G3.

(a) complete all relevant checks and procedures;

(b) perform prerotation;

(c) taxi a gyroplane;

(d) plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

(e) conduct a cross-wind take-off;

(f) conduct a short-field take-off;

(g) conduct a simulated rough or soft-field take-off;

(h) conduct climbs on constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following:

(i) best angle of climb (Vx);

(ii) best rate of climb (Vy);

(iii) cruise climb.

3.4 En route cruise

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code G3.

(a) maintain straight and level flight, and turn a gyroplane;

(b) navigate and transit from a circuit area to a training area and return;

(c) operate safely in local area airspace;

(d) establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following configurations:

(i) turbulence;

(ii) high speed.

3.5 Test specific activities and manoeuvres

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G5 and G6.

(a) enter and recover from each of the following flight conditions:

(i) a spiral descent;

(ii) level flight on the backside of the power curve;

(iii) flight behind the power curve;

(iv) conduct steep-level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

(b) manage an engine failure after take-off;

(c) conduct a precautionary search;

(d) manage the following malfunctions:

(i) a malfunction during start or shutdown;

(ii) any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i):

(A) an aircraft system malfunction;

(B) engine or cabin fire;

(C) radio failure;

(e) perform a forced landing.

3.6 Descent and arrival

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code G3.

(a) conduct descents maintaining constant heading and descending turns;

(b) plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

3.7 Circuit, approach and landing

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, G4 and G6.

(a) conduct normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

(b) conduct a cross-wind landing;

(c) conduct a short-field landing;

(d) perform a go-around procedure;

(e) perform after-landing actions and procedures.

3.8 Shutdown and post-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1 and C2.

(a) park, shutdown and secure a gyroplane;

(b) complete post-flight administration.

3.9 General requirements

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

(a) maintain an effective lookout;

(b) maintain situational awareness;

(c) assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

(d) set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

(e) maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

(f) recognise and manage threats;

(g) recognise and manage errors;

(h) recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

(i) communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the test;

(j) manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

(k) manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

(l) manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

4\. Operational scope and conditions

**4.1** For paragraph 1 (b), the following operational scope applies to the flight test:

(a) managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight;

(b) simulated carriage of passengers and cargo;

(c) simulated private local area operation;

(d) operating in Class G airspace at a non-towered aerodrome;

(e) emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the aircraft flight manual.

**4.2** For paragraph 1 (b), the following conditions apply to the flight test:

(a) activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures;

(b) must be conducted in a gyroplane;

(c) must be conducted by day under the VFR;

(d) operating at a non-towered aerodrome may be simulated if the test is conducted at a controlled aerodrome;

(e) if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the aircraft flight manual, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres can be taken from the applicant’s training records.

Appendix G.4 RPL Airship category rating flight test

**RESERVED**

The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a helicopter; conducted by day under the VFR; the flight must include: operating in Class G airspace and in controlled airspace; and operating at a non-towered aerodrome and a controlled aerodrome; if the area where the test is conducted does not have, or have available, controlled airspace or a controlled aerodrome, operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated as applicable; assessment of competency for activities and manoeuvres that require the applicant to operate the helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions may be taken from the applicant’s training records if the conditions are insufficient.

Appendix H.4 PPL Gyroplane category rating flight test

1\. Flight test requirements

An applicant for a private pilot licence with gyroplane category rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

(a) knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

(b) ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

2\. Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the following topics are listed:

(a) privileges and limitations of the private pilot licence with gyroplane category rating;

(b) applicability of drug and alcohol regulations;

(c) aircraft instrument requirements for VFR operations;

(d) emergency equipment requirements;

(e) requirements for landing areas and aerodromes;

(f) GNSS and its use in VFR navigation;

(g) fuel planning and oil requirements for the flight;

(h) loading and unloading fuel;

(i) managing passengers and the carriage of cargo;

(j) aircraft loading system;

(k) aircraft performance and landing calculations;

(l) pilot maintenance authorisations;

(m) gyroplane speed limitations;

(n) aircraft systems;

(o) activities and manoeuvres.

3\. Activities and manoeuvres

**3.1** For paragraph 1 (b), the activities and manoeuvres set out in subclauses 3.2 to 3.9 are mentioned.

*Note* The activities and manoeuvres are not required to be conducted in the order in which they appear in this Appendix.

3.2 Pre-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2, C4 and NAV.

(a) perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

(b) perform the pre-flight inspection;

(c) refuel a gyroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

3.3 Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G2, G3, C3 and NAV.

(a) complete all relevant checks and procedures;

(b) taxi a gyroplane;

(c) plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

(d) conduct a cross-wind take-off;

(e) conduct a short-field take-off;

(f) conduct climbs on constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following:

(i) best angle of climb (Vx);

(ii) best rate of climb (Vy);

(iii) cruise climb.

3.4 En route cruise

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, NAV and RNE.

(a) maintain straight and level flight, and turn gyroplane;

(b) navigate en route;

(c) establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions:

(i) turbulence;

(ii) holding;

(iii) range;

(d) navigate at low level;

(e) perform a lost recovery procedure;

(f) perform a diversion procedure;

(g) navigate using instrument navigation systems.

3.5 Test specific activities and manoeuvres

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G5, G6 and C3.

(a) enter and recover from each of the following flight conditions:

(i) a spiral descent;

(ii) level flight on the backside of the power curve;

(iii) flight behind the power curve;

(iv) conduct steep-level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

(b) manage an engine failure after take-off;

(c) conduct a precautionary search;

(d) manage the following malfunctions:

(i) a malfunction during start or shutdown;

(ii) any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i):

(A) an aircraft system malfunction;

(B) engine or cabin fire;

(C) radio failure;

(e) perform a forced landing.

3.6 Descent and arrival

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3 and NAV.

(a) conduct descents maintaining constant heading and descending turns;

(b) plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

3.7 Circuit, approach and landing

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, G4 and G6.

(a) conduct normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

(b) conduct a cross-wind landing;

(c) conduct short-field landing approaches and landings;

(d) perform a go-around procedure;

(e) perform after-landing actions and procedures.

3.8 Shutdown and post-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1 and C2.

(a) park, shutdown and secure a gyroplane;

(b) complete post-flight administration.

3.9 General requirements

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C1, C3, C4, C5, CTA, CTR, OGA, ONTA, NAV, NTS1 and NTS2.

(a) maintain an effective lookout;

(b) maintain situational awareness;

(c) assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

(d) set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

(e) maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

(f) recognise and manage threats;

(g) recognise and manage errors;

(h) recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

(i) operate in controlled airspace;

(j) operate in Class G airspace;

(k) operate at a controlled aerodrome;

(l) operate at a non-towered aerodrome;

(m) communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the test;

(n) manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

(o) manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

(p) manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

4\. Operational scope and conditions

**4.1** For paragraph 1 (b), the following operational scope applies to the flight test:

(a) managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight;

(b) simulated carriage of passengers and cargo;

(c) simulated private cross-country operation;

(d) operating in Class G and controlled airspace;

(e) emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the aircraft flight manual.

**4.2** For paragraph 1 (b), the following conditions apply to the flight test:

(a) activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures;

(b) must be conducted in a gyroplane;

(c) must be conducted by day under the VFR;

(d) the flight must include:

(i) operating in Class G airspace and in controlled airspace; and

(ii) operating at a non-towered aerodrome and a controlled aerodrome;

(e) if the area where the test is conducted does not have controlled airspace or a controlled aerodrome, or they are unavailable, operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated, as applicable;

(f) if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the aircraft flight manual, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres can be taken from the applicant’s training records.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IFF, IFL and TR-MEA.

perform full and limited panel instrument flying;

recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes, including the following: 1 recovery using a full instrument panel; 1 recovery using a limited instrument panel;

manage an engine failure during take-off with IAS greater than or equal to V1;

conduct an instrument departure with 1 engine inoperative;

*Note* For clarity, this manoeuvre must be separate to the manoeuvre required in paragraph (f), namely a missed approach.

conduct an instrument approach with 1 engine inoperative;

conduct a missed approach procedure with 1 engine inoperative;

manage at least 1 of the following: a system malfunction; fire; radio failure.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IAP2, IAP3 and TR-MEA.

perform a descent or published arrival procedure to an aerodrome;

track to the holding fix position and conduct a holding pattern or sector 3 entry procedure;

prepare for conducting a 2D instrument approach operation;

conduct a 2D instrument approach operation;

prepare for conducting a 3D instrument approach operation;

conduct a 3D instrument approach operation;

conduct a missed approach procedure for at least 1 instrument approach operation.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR and TR-MEA.

conduct a visual circling approach involving a change of heading to the runway of at least 90˚, if required;

conduct a cross-wind approach and landing;

land and perform after landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code C2.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C3, C5, CTA, CTR, MCO, NAV, NTS1, NTS2, ONTA and OGA.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

operate effectively as a crew member;

demonstrate effective leadership and authority;

maintain multi-crew situational awareness;

make effective decisions;

operate in controlled airspace;

operate in Class G airspace;

operate at a controlled aerodrome;

operate at a non-towered aerodrome;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: operate and monitor all aircraft systems that are available from the control seat the applicant occupies; perform the functions of co-pilot in the pilot flying and pilot monitoring roles using checks and procedures applicable to a multi-crew operation; conduct the operation as an IFR simulated commercial operation; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a multi-engine turbine aeroplane, or a flight simulator approved for the purpose, which is configured and equipped for multi-crew operations; operated using multi-crew standard operating procedures; conducted under the IFR including the following: an instrument departure; at least 2 different kinds of instrument approach procedure; at least one 2D instrument approach operation; an ILS or GLS instrument approach operation; at least 1 missed approach procedure commencing at the MDA or DA as applicable or a higher altitude if appropriate for safety or operational reasons; if the applicant is not the holder of a multi-engine aeroplane instrument endorsement, a visual circling approach involving a change of heading to the runway of at least 90˚; the flight must include: operating in Class G airspace and in controlled airspace; and operating at a non-towered aerodrome and at a controlled aerodrome; if the area where the test is conducted does not have, or have available, controlled airspace or a towered aerodrome, operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated as applicable. If the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (c) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Section K Air transport pilot licence (ATPL)Appendix K.1 ATPL Aeroplane category rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for an air transport pilot licence with aeroplane category rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the air transport pilot licence with aeroplane category rating;

requirements for an AOC;

classification of operations;

type of information contained in an operations manual;

flight and duty time limits;

applicability of drug and alcohol regulations;

aircraft instrument requirements;

emergency equipment requirements;

requirements for landing areas and aerodromes;

fuel planning and oil requirements for the flight;

managing passengers and the carriage of cargo;

aircraft loading system;

aircraft performance and landing calculations;

pilot maintenance authorisations;

aircraft speed limitations;

aircraft systems.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-Flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2, C4, CIR and TR-MEA.

plan an IFR flight;

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes TR-MEA and CIR.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

taxi an aeroplane;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a published instrument departure if available, otherwise in accordance with an ATC clearance (all engines);

conduct climb profiles and climbing turns.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR and TR-MEA.

navigate en route using ground-based and satellite-based navigation systems;

perform integrity checks for ground-based and satellite-based navigation systems;

identify and avoid hazardous weather conditions;

establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions: turbulence; holding; range.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IFF, IFL and TR-MEA.

perform instrument flying using normal and stand-by instrument displays;

recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes, including the following: 1 recovery using a normal display; 1 recovery using a stand-by instrument display;

manage an engine failure during take-off with IAS greater than or equal to V1;

conduct an instrument departure procedure with 1 engine inoperative;

*Note* For clarity, this manoeuvre must be separate to the manoeuvre required in paragraph (f), namely a missed approach.

conduct an instrument approach procedure with 1 engine inoperative;

conduct a missed approach procedure with 1 engine inoperative;

manage at least 1 of the following that is not included in another item in subclause 3.4: a system malfunction; fire; radio failure.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IAP2, IAP3 and TR-MEA.

perform a descent or published arrival procedure to an aerodrome;

track to the holding fix position and conduct a holding pattern or sector 3 entry procedure;

prepare for conducting a 2D instrument approach operation;

conduct a 2D approach operation;

prepare for conducting a 3D instrument approach operation;

conduct a 3D instrument approach operation;

conduct a missed approach procedure for at least 1 instrument approach operation.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR and TR-MEA.

if applicable, conduct a visual circling approach;

land and perform after landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code C2.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C3, C5, CTA, CTR, MCO, NTS1, NTS2, OGA, ONTA and TR‑MEA.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

operate effectively as a crew member;

as pilot in command, demonstrate effective leadership and authority;

maintain multi-crew situational awareness;

make effective decisions as the pilot in command;

operate in controlled airspace;

operate in Class G airspace (only if the flight test involves operating in Class G airspace);

operate at a controlled aerodrome;

operate at a non-towered aerodrome (only if the flight test involves operating at a non-towered aerodrome);

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: operate and monitor all aircraft systems that are available from the control seat the applicant occupies; perform the functions of pilot in command in the pilot flying and pilot monitoring roles using checks and procedures applicable to a multi-crew operation; conduct a multi-crew operation as an IFR simulated commercial operation; operate in controlled airspace; operate at a controlled aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a multi-engine turbine aeroplane, or a flight simulator approved for the purpose, which is configured and equipped for multi-crew operations; for paragraph 3.1 (a), the applicant may use a system-generated flight plan; operated using multi-crew standard operating procedures; conducted under the IFR, including the following: an instrument departure; at least 2 different kinds of instrument approach procedure; at least one 2D instrument approach operation; an ILS or GLS instrument approach operation; at least 1 missed approach procedure commencing at the MDA or DA as applicable or a higher altitude if appropriate for safety or operational reasons; at least 1 instrument approach operation without the autopilot or flight director being used; if the applicant is not the holder of a multi-engine aeroplane instrument endorsement, a visual circling approach involving a change of heading to the runway of at least 90˚; the flight must include sectors in controlled airspace and at a controlled aerodrome, and may include operations in Class G airspace and at a non‑towered aerodrome; if the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (c) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix K.2 ATPL Helicopter category rating flight test Flight test requirements An applicant for an air transport pilot licence with helicopter category rating flight test must demonstrate the following: knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2; ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test. Provision is made in clauses 3 and 4 for the test to be conducted under the VFR or IFR. For the test to be conducted under the IFR, the applicant must hold an instrument rating with the relevant aircraft category/class endorsement and instrument approach endorsements. classification of operations;

type of information contained in an operations manual;

flight and duty time limits;

aircraft instrument requirements;

pilot maintenance authorisations;

aircraft speed limitations;

aircraft systems.

navigate en route;

land on and lift off from sloping ground;

execute a limited power take-off, approach and landing;

land, manoeuvre, and take off from 1 of the following: a confined area; a pinnacle; ridge line;

manage a control or tail rotor malfunction in flight and at the hover;

conduct a circling approach, if required;

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code C2.

park, shutdown and secure a helicopter;

complete post-flight administration.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes, C1, C3, C4, C5, CTA, CTR, MCO, NAV, NTS1, NTS2, ONTA, OGA and TR-SEH or TR-MEH (as applicable).

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: operate and monitor all aircraft systems; perform the functions of pilot in command in the pilot flying and pilot monitoring roles using checks and procedures applicable to a multi-crew operation; conduct the operation as a simulated commercial VFR or IFR operation; operate in controlled airspace; operate at a controlled aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a sufficiently complex multi-engine or single-engine turbine helicopter, or a flight simulator approved for the purpose, which is configured and equipped for multi-crew operations; operated using multi-crew standard operating procedures; except as provided in paragraph (f), conducted by day under the VFR; the flight must include the following: operating in Class G airspace and in controlled airspace; operating at a non-towered and a controlled aerodrome; if the applicant is the holder of an instrument rating and chooses to perform the test under the IFR, then he or she must demonstrate competency by performing the following: at least 2 different kinds of instrument approach procedures; at least one 2D instrument approach operation; an ILS or GLS instrument approach procedure; at least 1 missed approach procedure commencing at the MDA or DA as applicable, or a higher altitude if appropriate for safety or operational reasons; at least 1 instrument approach operation without the autopilot or flight director being used; if the flight test is conducted in an area that does not have, or have available, controlled airspace or a controlled aerodrome, operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated as applicable; if the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (c) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Section L Aircraft ratings Appendix L.1 Single-engine aeroplane class rating flight test Flight test requirements An applicant for a single-engine aeroplane class rating flight test must demonstrate the following: knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2; ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test. An applicant who completes a flight test in an aeroplane covered by the single‑engine aeroplane class rating and meets the flight test standard for the grant of a pilot licence with aeroplane category rating is taken to meet these flight test requirements. Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the class rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection;

refuel an aeroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A2, A3 and IFF.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

taxi an aeroplane;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a cross-wind take-off;

conduct a short-field take-off;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns in at least 2 of the following performance configurations: cruise climb; maximum rate climb; maximum angle climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn an aeroplane;

navigate and transit from an aerodrome circuit area to a training area and return;

operate safely in local area airspace;

establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions: turbulence; flaps selected; high speed.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A5, A6 and IFF.

enter and recover from each of the following, 1 of which must be in the approach configuration: a fully developed stall; a wing drop at the stall;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes;

manage an engine failure after take-off;

manage the following malfunctions: a malfunction during start or shutdown; any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i): an aircraft system malfunction; engine or cabin fire; radio failure;

perform a forced landing.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

conduct descents and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, A4 and A6.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct a cross-wind landing;

conduct short-field and flapless landings;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1 and C2.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for airspace being used during the test;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the test;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; simulated carriage of passengers and cargo; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in: an aeroplane that is covered by the single-engine aeroplane class rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; conducted by day under the VFR; if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the AFM, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres may be taken from the applicant’s training records; if the flight test is conducted in an FSTD, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (a) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

An applicant who completes a flight test in a helicopter covered by the single‑engine helicopter class rating and meets the flight test standard for the grant of a pilot licence with helicopter category rating is taken to meet these flight test requirements. privileges and limitations of the class rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection;

refuel a helicopter (may be assessed by questioning).

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H1, H2, H3, H4, H5.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

lift-off and hover a helicopter;

taxi a helicopter;

air transit a helicopter;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following: maximum rate climb; maximum (best) angle climb; cruise climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code H5.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn a helicopter;

navigate and transit from a circuit area to a training area and return;

operate safely in local area airspace.

**Test specific manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H2, H6 and H7.

hover a helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions and perform turns around 1 of the following: rotor mast; helicopter nose; helicopter tail;

perform sidewards and backwards flight;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform an autorotative flight manoeuvre;

land on and lift off from sloping ground;

land, manoeuvre, and take off in a confined area;

execute a limited power take-off, approach and landing;

perform a forced landing;

manage an engine failure during hover or taxi;

manage a control or tail rotor malfunction in flight and at the hover;

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code H5.

conduct descents and descending turns;

plan and conduct an aerodrome or helicopter landing site arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes H3, H4 and H5.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct an approach to the hover;

conduct a helicopter air transit;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and H1.

park, shutdown and secure a helicopter;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C1, C3, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system that is not required for the flight is not an assessable item unless it is used by the applicant; simulated carriage of passengers and cargo; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a helicopter that is covered by the single-engine helicopter class rating; conducted in: a helicopter that is covered by the single-engine helicopter class rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; conducted by day under the VFR; assessment of competency for activities and manoeuvres that require the applicant to operate the helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions may be taken from the applicant’s training records if the conditions are insufficient.

Appendix L.3 Single-engine gyroplane class rating flight test

1\. Flight test requirements

**1.1** An applicant for a single-engine gyroplane class rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

(a) knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

(b) ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

**1.2** An applicant who completes a flight test in a gyroplane covered by the single-engine gyroplane class rating and meets the flight test standard for the grant of a pilot licence with gyroplane category rating is taken to meet these flight test requirements.

2\. Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1.1 (a), the following topics are listed:

(a) privileges and limitations of the class rating;

(b) flight review requirements;

(c) navigation and operating systems;

(d) normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

(e) operating limitations;

(f) weight and balance limitations;

(g) aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

(h) flight planning.

3\. Activities and manoeuvres

**3.1** For paragraph 1.1 (b), the activities and manoeuvres set out in subclauses 3.2 to 3.9 are mentioned.

*Note* The activities and manoeuvres are not required to be conducted in the order in which they appear in this Appendix.

3.2 Pre-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and C4.

(a) perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

(b) perform a pre-flight inspection;

(c) refuel a gyroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

3.3 Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G2 and G3.

(a) complete all relevant checks and procedures;

(b) taxi a gyroplane;

(c) plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

(d) conduct a cross-wind take-off;

(e) conduct a short-field take-off;

(f) conduct climbs on constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following performance configurations:

(i) best angle of climb (Vx);

(ii) best rate of climb (Vy);

(iii) cruise climb.

3.4 En route cruise

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code G3.

(a) maintain straight and level flight, and turn a gyroplane;

(b) navigate and transit from an aerodrome circuit area to a training area and return;

(c) operate safely in local area airspace;

(d) establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions:

(i) turbulence;

(ii) high speed.

3.5 Test specific activities and manoeuvres

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1, G5 and G6.

(a) enter and recover from each of the following, 1 of which must be in the approach configuration:

(i) a spiral descent;

(ii) flight behind the power curve/minimum level flight speed;

(b) conduct steep-level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

(c) manage an engine failure after take-off;

(d) manage the following malfunctions:

(i) a malfunction during start or shutdown;

(ii) any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i):

(A) an aircraft system malfunction;

(B) engine or cabin fire;

(C) radio failure;

(e) perform a forced landing.

3.6 Descent and arrival

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code G3.

(a) conduct descents and descending turns;

(b) plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

3.7 Circuit, approach and landing

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, G4 and G6.

(a) conduct normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

(b) conduct a cross-wind landing;

(c) conduct short-field landings;

(d) conduct simulated rough or soft-field take-off;

(e) perform a go-around procedure;

(f) perform after-landing actions and procedures.

3.8 Shutdown and post-flight

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G1 and C2.

(a) park, shutdown and secure a gyroplane;

(b) complete post-flight administration.

3.9 General requirements

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes G3, C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

(a) maintain an effective lookout;

(b) maintain situational awareness;

(c) assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

(d) set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

(e) maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

(f) recognise and manage threats;

(g) recognise and manage errors;

(h) recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

(i) communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for airspace being used during the test;

(j) manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

(k) manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the test;

(l) manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

4\. Operational scope and conditions

**4.1** For paragraph 1.1 (b), the following operational scope applies to the flight test:

(a) managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight;

(b) simulated carriage of passengers and cargo;

(c) simulated private local area operation;

(d) operating in Class G airspace, at a non-towered aerodrome;

(e) emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the aircraft flight manual.

**4.2** For paragraph 1.1 (b), the following conditions apply to the flight test:

(a) activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures;

(b) conducted in:

(i) a gyroplane that is covered by the single-engine gyroplane class rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or

(ii) a flight simulator approved for the purpose;

(c) conducted by day under the VFR;

(d) if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the aircraft flight manual, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres can be taken from the applicant’s training records.

Appendix L.4 Airship class rating flight test

**RESERVED**

Appendix L.5 Multi-engine aeroplane class rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a multi-engine aeroplane class rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the class rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2 and AME.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection;

refuel an aeroplane (may be assessed by questioning).

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A2, A3, AME and IFF.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

taxi an aeroplane;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a cross-wind take-off;

conduct a short-field take-off;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns in at least 2 of the following performance configurations: cruise climb; maximum rate climb; maximum angle climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn aeroplane;

operate the aeroplane in the cruise configuration for 1 of the following conditions: turbulence; holding; range;

navigate using instrument navigation systems.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1, A4, A5, AME and IFF.

enter and recover from a stall in the approach configuration and at least 1 other configuration;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes;

manage an engine failure after take-off;

manage an engine failure in the cruise configuration;

conduct an approach and landing with 1 engine inoperative;

conduct a missed approach with 1 engine inoperative;

manage the following malfunctions: a malfunction during start or shutdown; any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i): an aircraft system malfunction; engine or cabin fire; radio failure.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code A3.

conduct descents and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, A4 and AME.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct a cross-wind landing;

conduct short-field and flapless landings;

perform a go-around procedure with all engines operating;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A1 and C2.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes A3, AME, C1, C4, C5, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft state;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight;

manage passengers and the carriage of cargo.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; operate the aircraft under normal, non-normal and emergency conditions with particular attention given to conditions associated with asymmetric engine performance; simulated carriage of passengers and cargo; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in: an aeroplane that is covered by the multi-engine aeroplane class rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; conducted by day under the VFR; if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the AFM, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres may be taken from the applicant’s training records; if the flight test is conducted in an FSTD, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (b) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix L.6 Single-engine aeroplane type rating flight test Flight test requirements An applicant for a single-engine aeroplane type rating flight test must demonstrate the following: knowledge of the topics listed in subclause 2.1; ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test. For paragraph 61.790 (a), if the flight test for the rating is conducted under the IFR, the applicant must demonstrate his or her knowledge of the items in subclause 2.2 and his or her competency in the activities and manoeuvres in clause 3, as they apply to operating the aircraft under the IFR. Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the type rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes TR-SEA and CIR for IFR operations.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

taxi the aeroplane;

plan, brief and conduct a take-off and the following as applicable: for a VFR operation, VFR departure procedures; for an IFR operation, an instrument departure;

conduct a cross-wind take-off;

conduct climb profiles and climbing turns.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes TR-SEA and CIR for IFR operations.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn an aeroplane;

establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions: turbulence; holding configuration; range;

navigate using instrument navigation systems.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes TR-SEA and CIR for IFR operations.

conduct 2 approach to the stall and recovery manoeuvres, 1 of which must be in the approach configuration and 1 in any other configuration;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 unusual attitude manoeuvres;

manage an engine failure after take-off;

manage the following malfunctions: a malfunction during start or shutdown; any 1 of the following that is not performed under subparagraph (i): an aircraft system malfunction; engine or cabin fire; radio failure;

perform a forced landing.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEA and for IFR operations in unit codes CIR and IAP2.

conduct descent profiles and descending turns;

complete 1 of the following: for a VFR operation, plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures; for an IFR operation, plan and conduct the following: an instrument arrival; a 2D instrument approach procedure; a missed approach procedure.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEA.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct a cross-wind landing;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEA.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NTS1, NTS2, TR-SEA, and CIR for IFR operations.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the grant of the type rating, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM; for subclause 1.2, the flight has 2 components and includes knowledge and activities and manoeuvres for operating the aircraft under the VFR and under the IFR as follows: the component for VFR operations includes general handling manoeuvres; the component for IFR operations includes the standards required to conduct an IFR operation in a single-engine aeroplane covered by the type rating. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in 1 of the following: an aeroplane that is covered by the type rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; except for paragraph (e), conducted by day under the VFR; if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the AFM, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres may be taken from the applicant’s training records; for subclause 1.2, the flight test includes conducting an IFR operation; if the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (b) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix L.7 Single-engine helicopter type rating flight test Flight test requirements An applicant for a single-engine helicopter type rating flight test must demonstrate the following: knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2; ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test. An applicant who completes a flight test in a helicopter covered by a single‑engine helicopter type rating and meets the flight test standard for the grant of a pilot licence with helicopter category rating is taken to meet these flight test requirements. Knowledge requirements

privileges and limitations of the type rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

lift-off and hover a helicopter;

taxi a helicopter;

air transit a helicopter;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a maximum performance take-off;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following: maximum rate climb; maximum (best) angle climb; cruise climb.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn a helicopter;

navigate using instrument navigation systems.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

hover helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions and perform turns around 1 of the following: rotor mast; helicopter nose; helicopter tail;

perform autorotative flight manoeuvres;

land on and lift off from sloping ground;

execute a limited power take-off, approach and landing;

perform a forced landing from level flight;

manage an engine failure during hover or taxi;

manage a control or tail rotor malfunction in flight and at the hover;

manage at least 1 of the following: an engine fire; electrical failure; hydraulic system malfunction; airframe fuel system malfunction; engine governor system malfunction.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

conduct descents and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome or helicopter landing site arrival and circuit joining procedures.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct approach to the hover;

conduct helicopter air transit;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-SEH.

park, shutdown and secure a helicopter;

complete post-flight administration.

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NTS1, NTS2 and TR-SEH.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for airspace;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system that is not required for the flight is not an assessable item unless it is used by the applicant; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in a helicopter that is covered by the type rating or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; conducted by day under the VFR; assessment of competency for activities and manoeuvres that require the applicant to operate the helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions may be taken from the applicant’s training records if the conditions are insufficient; if the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (b) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.
