manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the grant of the type rating, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM; for subclause 1.2, the flight has 2 components and includes knowledge and activities and manoeuvres for operating the aircraft under the VFR and under the IFR. the component for VFR operations includes general handling manoeuvres; the component for IFR operations includes the standards required to conduct an IFR operation in a multi-engine aeroplane covered by the type rating. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in 1 of the following: an aeroplane that is covered by the type rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; except for paragraph (e), conducted by day under the VFR; if the aerodrome cross-wind conditions for the runway used during the test are less than 70% of the maximum in the AFM, evidence that the applicant has demonstrated competency performing cross-wind take-off and landing manoeuvres may be taken from the applicant’s training records; for subclause 1.2, the flight test includes conducting an IFR operation; if the flight test is conducted in an FSTD, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (b) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix L.9 Multi-engine helicopter type rating flight test Flight test requirements An applicant for a multi engine helicopter type rating flight test must demonstrate the following: knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2.1; ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test. For paragraph 61.790 (a), if the flight test for the rating is conducted under the IFR, the applicant must demonstrate his or her knowledge of the items in subclause 2.2 and his or her competency in the activities and manoeuvres in clause 3, as they apply to operating the aircraft under the IFR. Knowledge requirements For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following topics: privileges and limitations of the type rating; flight review requirements; navigation and operating systems; normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures; operating limitations; weight and balance limitations; aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data; flight planning. For subclause 1.2, the additional topics are the following: privileges and limitations of the type rating with respect to conducting IFR operations; navigation and flight management systems; conducting IFR operations in a helicopter covered by the rating. Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-Flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

perform pre-flight actions and procedures;

perform a pre-flight inspection.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

lift-off and hover a helicopter;

taxi a helicopter;

air transit a helicopter;

plan, brief and conduct a take-off and the following as applicable: for a VFR operation, VFR departure procedures; for an IFR operation, an instrument departure procedure;

conduct a maximum performance take-off;

conduct climbs on a constant heading and climbing turns, including at least 2 of the following: maximum rate climb; maximum (best) angle climb; cruise climb.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn a helicopter;

navigate using instrument navigation systems.

**Test specific manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

hover helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions and perform turns around 1 of the following: rotor mast; helicopter nose; helicopter tail;

perform sidewards and backwards flight;

conduct steep level turns of at least 45˚ angle of bank;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 unusual attitude manoeuvres;

land on and lift off from sloping ground;

execute a limited power take-off, approach and landing;

manage an engine failure – at least 1 from take-off, cruise flight or approach and landing;

manage an engine failure during hover or taxi;

manage a control or tail rotor malfunction in flight and at the hover;

manage at least 1 of the following: an engine fire; electrical failure; hydraulic system malfunction; airframe fuel system malfunction; engine governor system malfunction.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

conduct descent profiles and descending turns;

complete 1 of the following: for a VFR operation, plan and conduct an aerodrome or helicopter landing site arrival and circuit joining procedures; for an IFR operation, plan and conduct the following: an instrument arrival; a 2D instrument approach procedure; a missed approach procedure.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct an approach to the hover;

conduct a helicopter air transit;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-MEH.

park, shutdown and secure a helicopter;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NTS1, NTS2 and TR-MEH.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft state;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for airspace;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage fuel system and monitor fuel plan and usage.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system that is not required for the flight is not an assessable item unless it is used by the applicant; if the type rating is for a multi-crew certified helicopter, the roles of Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring must be demonstrated by the applicant; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM; for subclause 1.2, the flight has 2 components and includes knowledge and activities and manoeuvres for operating the aircraft under the VFR and under the IFR as follows: the component for VFR operations includes general handling manoeuvres; the component for IFR operations includes the standards required to conduct an IFR operation in a multi-engine helicopter covered by the type rating. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in 1 of the following: a multi-engine helicopter covered by the type rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or an FSTD approved for the purpose; except for paragraph (e), conducted by day; assessment of competency for activities and manoeuvres that require the applicant to operate the helicopter in cross-wind and tailwind conditions may be taken from the applicant’s training records if the conditions are insufficient; for subclause 1.2, the flight test includes conducting an IFR operation; if the flight test is conducted in an FSTD, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: paragraph 3.1 (c) — perform a pre-flight inspection; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix L.10 Cruise relief co-pilot rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a cruise relief co-pilot rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS which are relevant to the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following:

privileges and limitations of the type rating;

flight review requirements;

navigation and operating systems;

normal, abnormal and emergency flight procedures;

operating limitations;

weight and balance limitations;

aircraft performance data, including take-off and landing performance data;

flight planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

Perform pre-flight actions and procedures.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

Conduct climb profiles and climbing turns.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

maintain straight and level flight, and turn aeroplane;

establish and maintain cruise flight for at least 1 of the following conditions: turbulence; holding; range;

navigate using instrument navigation systems.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

conduct 2 approaches to the stall and recovery manoeuvres, 1 of which must be in the approach configuration and 1 in any other configuration;

perform full panel instrument flying;

using a full instrument panel, recover from at least 2 unusual attitude manoeuvres;

manage an engine failure in flight;

conduct an approach to land with 1 engine inoperative;

conduct a missed approach to land with 1 engine inoperative;

manage a malfunction of any aircraft system other than one that has been applied in paragraphs 3.4 (d) to (f).

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

conduct descent profiles and descending turns;

plan and conduct aerodrome arrival and circuit joining procedures.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

conduct a cross-wind landing;

perform a go-around procedure;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code TR-CR.

park, shutdown and secure an aeroplane;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NTS1, NTS2 and TR-CR.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the grant of the type rating, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM. The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in: an aeroplane that is covered by the type rating, except where the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulator in accordance with subregulation 61.245 (2); or a flight simulator that is approved for the purpose; conducted as an IFR operation; if the flight test is conducted in a flight simulator, the following activities may be assessed by oral questioning: subclause 3.1 — Pre-flight; subclause 3.7 — Shut down and post-flight.

Appendix L.12 Cruise relief flight engineer rating

**RESERVED**

Section M Instrument ratingAppendix M.1 Instrument rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for an instrument rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2 that are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the test;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS, which are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following topics:

privileges and limitations of the instrument rating and each instrument endorsement covered by the flight test;

proficiency check requirements;

IFR and approach recent experience requirements;

night recent experience requirements;

night VFR operations;

aircraft instrument requirements;

interpreting operational and meteorological information;

take-off minima;

holding and alternate requirements;

IFR procedures for all airspace classifications;

departure and approach instrument procedures;

operations below LSALT and MSA for day and night operations;

GNSS and PBN standards;

circling approaches;

adverse weather operations;

ERSA normal and emergency procedures;

IFR planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code CIR.

plan an IFR flight;

perform pre-flight actions and procedures.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR and IFF.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct an instrument departure and, if available, in accordance with: a published procedure; or an ATC clearance.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code CIR.

navigate en route using ground-based and satellite-based navigation systems;

perform ground-based and satellite-based navigation system integrity checks;

identify and avoid hazardous weather conditions (may be simulated).

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IFF and IFL.

perform full panel and limited panel instrument flying;

recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes, including the following: 1 recovery using a full instrument panel; 1 recovery using a limited instrument panel;

for a test in a multi-engine aircraft, conduct an instrument departure with 1 engine inoperative;

*Note* For clarity, this manoeuvre must be separate to the manoeuvre required in paragraph (e), namely a missed approach.

for a test in a multi-engine aircraft, conduct an instrument approach with 1 engine inoperative;

for a test in a multi-engine aircraft, with 1 engine inoperative, conduct 1 of the following: a missed approach procedure; a visual circling procedure.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IAP2, and IAP3.

perform a descent or published arrival procedure to an aerodrome;

track to the holding fix position and conduct a holding pattern or sector 3 entry procedure, and if the approach procedure is an RNAV/(GNSS) approach, then the holding pattern or sector 3 entry procedure must be for the RNAV/(GNSS) procedure;

for 2 different kinds of instrument approach procedure, conduct 2D instrument approach operations as follows: prepare for each operation; conduct the operation;

if required for the test — conduct a 3D instrument approach operation as follows: prepare for the operation; conduct the operation;

conduct a missed approach procedure.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code CIR.

conduct a visual circling approach involving a change of heading to the runway of at least 90˚;

perform after-landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code CIR.

park, shutdown and secure the aircraft;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, NTS1 and NTS2.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the test;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions

*Note* Reference to the same kind of relevant aircraft in this section has the same meaning as relevant aircraft in subregulation 61.880 (9) of Part 61 of CASR 1998.

**The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; an IFR operation; conduct an IFR departure, en route sectors, IFR arrival, 2D instrument approach and missed approach procedure; operating under the IFR: in the following: Class G airspace; controlled airspace; and at the following: a non-towered aerodrome; a controlled aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM.**

**The following conditions apply to the flight test and the applicant as applicable: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in an appropriate aircraft, except in accordance with subregulation 61.885 (4) where it is conducted in a flight simulator approved for the purpose; if the flight test is for the grant of an instrument rating, demonstrate competency conducting 2D instrument approach operations for at least 2 different kinds of 2D instrument approach procedures in the same relevant kind of aircraft; if the flight test is for the grant of an additional aircraft category/class instrument endorsement, demonstrate competency conducting at least one 2D instrument approach operation in the same relevant kind of aircraft; if the flight test is for the grant of a 3D instrument approach operation endorsement, demonstrate competency conducting an ILS or GLS instrument approach procedure; for paragraphs (d) and (e), demonstrating competency conducting instrument approach operations includes conducting a missed approach procedure for at least 1 approach operation, from the decision altitude or minimum descent altitude, as applicable, unless for safety or operational reasons a higher altitude is applied; for paragraph (f), demonstrate competency performing at least 1 instrument approach operation while manually manipulating the flight and power controls; if the flight test is conducted in an aircraft, it must be certified for operations conducted under the IFR and be appropriately equipped according to the requirements for each instrument endorsement the test is for; the flight must include: operating in Class G airspace; and operating at a non-towered aerodrome; operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated.**

Section N Private instrument ratingAppendix N.1 Private instrument rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a private instrument rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2 that are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the test;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS, which are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following topics:

privileges and limitations of the private instrument rating and the private instrument endorsement(s) covered by the flight test;

flight review requirements;

recency requirements;

night recency requirements;

night VFR operations;

aircraft instrument requirements;

interpreting operational and meteorological information;

take-off minima;

holding and alternate requirements;

IFR procedures for all airspace classifications;

departure and approach instrument procedures;

operations below LSALT and MSA for day and night operations;

GNSS and PBN standards;

circling approaches;

adverse weather operations;

ERSA normal and emergency procedures;

IFR planning.

Activities and manoeuvres

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes C2, C4, CIR and PIF.

plan an IFR flight;

perform pre-flight actions and procedures.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IFF and PIF.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

for a departure endorsement, plan, brief and conduct an instrument departure;

for a standard instrument departure (SID) endorsement, perform a SID or published departure procedure.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code PIF.

for each navigation endorsement being assessed during the test — navigate en route using the applicable ground-based and satellite-based navigation systems;

perform ground-based and satellite-based navigation system integrity checks;

identify and avoid hazardous weather conditions (may be simulated);

for each navigation endorsement covered by the flight test — using guidance information from the applicable navigation system, track to the holding fix and conduct a holding pattern or sector 3 entry procedure.

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IFF, IFL, NVR and PIF.

perform full panel instrument flying;

if the flight test is for the grant of the rating, do the following: perform limited panel instrument flying; recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes, including the following: 1 recovery using a full instrument panel; 1 recovery using a limited instrument panel;

for a multi-engine aircraft departure endorsement — conduct an instrument departure with 1 engine inoperative;

*Note* For clarity, this manoeuvre must be separate to the manoeuvre required in paragraph (e), namely a missed approach.

for an approach/arrival category specific endorsement — in a multi-engine aircraft of the applicable category, with 1 engine inoperative: conduct an instrument approach; and conduct 1 of the following: a missed approach; a visual circling procedure;

for the category specific night endorsement, in an aircraft of the applicable category: control the aircraft on the ground at night; and conduct normal circuit patterns and landings at night with and without landing lights; and manage a cockpit lighting failure; and perform a go-around at night.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, IAP2, IAP3 and PIF.

perform a descent to establish and maintain VMC above or at the LSALT or MSA;

perform a visual approach;

for a STAR endorsement — conduct a published STAR procedure;

for the approach/arrival endorsements include in the test — using the applicable published procedure, conduct the following: for each approach endorsement, an instrument approach procedure; for at least 1 approach endorsement, the applicable missed approach procedure; for at least 1 approach endorsement, a visual circling approach involving a change of heading to the runway of at least 90°.

**Circuit, approach and landing**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code PIF.

conduct a normal circuit pattern, approach and landing;

perform after landing actions and procedures.

**Shut down and post-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit code PIF.

park, shutdown and secure the aircraft;

complete post-flight administration.

**General requirements**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes CIR, NTS1, NTS2 and PIF.

maintain an effective lookout;

maintain situational awareness;

assess situations and make appropriate decisions;

set priorities and manage tasks effectively;

maintain effective communication and interpersonal relationships;

recognise and manage threats;

recognise and manage errors;

recognise and manage undesired aircraft states;

communicate effectively using appropriate procedures for the airspace being used during the flight;

manage the aircraft systems required for the flight;

manage the fuel system and monitor the fuel plan and fuel usage during the flight.

Operational scope and conditions

*Note* A reference to the same kind of relevant aircraft in this section has the same meaning as relevant aircraft in subregulation 61. 880 (9) of Part 61 of CASR 1998.

**The following operational scope applies to the flight test: managing an aircraft system, which is not required for the flight, is not an assessable item unless the applicant uses the system during the flight; conduct a private IFR operation; a flight test for the grant of a private IFR rating: must cover the requirements for the grant of the following: 1 of the aircraft category and class private instrument endorsements mentioned in Part 1 of Table 61.935; 1 of the navigation endorsements mentioned in Part 2 of Table 61.935; and can include the requirements for any other private instrument endorsement that is relevant for the aircraft in which the flight test is conducted; depending on which private instrument endorsements are being assessed, operating an appropriate category and class of aircraft under the IFR as follows: for the grant of an aircraft category and class private instrument endorsement mentioned in Part 1 of Table 61.935 — navigating en route, perform an entry and holding procedure using at least 1 instrument navigation system; for the grant of a navigation endorsement mentioned in Part 2 of Table 61.935 — navigating en route, perform an entry and holding procedure using the navigation system for the endorsement; for the grant of a departure endorsement mentioned in Part 3 of Table 61.935 — conduct an instrument departure, other than a standard instrument departure; for the grant of an approach and arrival endorsement mentioned in Part 4 of Table 61.935: for the grant of the STAR endorsement — conduct an arrival using a procedure published in the AIP; and for the grant of any other endorsement in Part 4 of the table — conduct an instrument approach operation using the applicable navigation system; for the grant of a category specific approach and arrival endorsement mentioned in Part 5 of Table 61.935 — conduct an instrument approach operation in a multi-engine aircraft of the applicable category; for the grant of the night private instrument endorsement mentioned in Part 6 of Table 61.935 — conduct an operation at night in an aircraft of the specified category; operating under the IFR: in the following: Class G airspace; controlled airspace; and at the following: a non-towered aerodrome; a controlled aerodrome; emergencies and abnormal situations relating to aircraft systems, powerplants and the airframe are simulated and limited to those described in the AFM.**

**The following conditions apply to the flight test: activities and manoeuvres are performed in accordance with published procedures; conducted in an appropriate aircraft or a flight simulator approved for the purpose; if the test is for the grant of an approach endorsement, demonstrating competency conducting instrument approaches includes conducting a missed approach procedure for at least 1 approach operation, from the decision altitude or minimum descent altitude, as applicable, unless for safety or operational reasons a higher altitude is applied; for paragraph (c), demonstrate competency performing at least 1 instrument approach operation while manually manipulating the flight and power controls; if the flight test is conducted in an aircraft, it must be certified for operations conducted under the IFR and be appropriately equipped according to the requirements for each private instrument endorsement the test is for; the flight must include: operating in Class G airspace; and operating at a non-towered aerodrome; if the area where the test is conducted does not have, or have available, controlled airspace or a controlled aerodrome, operating in controlled airspace or at a controlled aerodrome may be simulated as applicable.**

Section O Night VFR ratingAppendix O.1 Night VFR rating flight test Flight test requirements

An applicant for a night VFR rating flight test must demonstrate the following:

knowledge of the topics listed in clause 2, which are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the test;

ability to conduct the activities and manoeuvres mentioned in clause 3, within the operational scope and under the conditions mentioned in clause 4, to the competency standards required under section 12 of this MOS, which are relevant to the endorsements that are being assessed during the flight test.

Knowledge requirements

For paragraph 1 (a), the topics are the following topics:

privileges and limitations of the night VFR rating and the night VFR endorsement that is covered by the flight test;

flight review requirements;

night recency requirements;

night VFR operations;

interpreting operational and meteorological information;

ground and aircraft lighting requirements;

use of instrument and navigation systems;

take-off minima;

holding and alternate requirements;

operational requirements and procedures for all airspace classifications;

operations below LSALT and MSA for night operations;

GNSS and PBN standards;

hazardous weather conditions;

ERSA normal and emergency procedures;

night VFR planning.

*Note* For paragraph 1 (b), the flight test includes all of the following activities and manoeuvres. The sequence set out here is not necessarily intended to direct the order of activities and manoeuvres.

**Pre-flight**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NVR2 and NVR3.

plan a night VFR flight;

perform pre-flight actions and procedures.

**Ground operations, take-off, departure and climb**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes IFF, NVR1, NVR2 and NVR3.

complete all relevant checks and procedures;

plan, brief and conduct take-off and departure procedures;

conduct a take-off and departure from an aerodrome which is remote from ground lighting.

**En route cruise**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NVR2 and NVR3.

navigate en route using visual tracking and visual position fixes;

navigate en route using ground-based and satellite-based navigation systems;

perform ground-based and satellite-based navigation system integrity checks;

identify and avoid hazardous weather conditions (may be simulated).

**Test specific activities and manoeuvres**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes IFF, IFL, NVR1, NVR2 and NVR3.

perform full panel and limited panel instrument flying;

recover from at least 2 different unusual aircraft attitudes, including the following: 1 recovery using a full instrument panel; 1 recovery using a limited instrument panel;

manage a cockpit lighting failure;

for the grant of a multi-engine aeroplane night VFR endorsement — manage an engine failure in a multi-engine aeroplane during the cruise;

for the grant of a multi-engine helicopter night VFR endorsement — manage an engine failure in a multi-engine helicopter during the cruise.

**Descent and arrival**

*Note* The relevant competency standards are in unit codes NVR2 and NVR3.

conduct a descent and perform a visual approach procedure to an aerodrome;

plan and conduct an arrival and circuit joining procedures.
